title: Most people never think about the soldier who pierced Jesus’ side.
paragraphs: Most people never think about the soldier who pierced Jesus’ side.

He appears in the story for only a moment.
No name.
No long speech.
Just a single action.
One thrust of a spear.
And yet that moment carries one of the most powerful lessons hidden in the crucifixion story.
John 19:34 says:
“But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.”
Think about that for a moment.

This soldier was not a follower of Jesus.
He was not a believer.
He was not mourning at the cross.
He was just doing his job.

Rome wanted confirmation that the man on the cross was dead.
So the soldier stepped forward with a spear and drove it into Jesus’ side.
But something happened in that moment that no one expected.
Blood and water flowed out.
Not just blood.
Blood and water.

John specifically records it because it mattered.
It was unusual.
It was significant.
It was a testimony.
Even in death, Jesus was still revealing something.
Even in His wounded body, there was still a message.
And here is the lesson that struck me.
The soldier came to confirm death.
But what flowed from Jesus revealed life.
That soldier came close to Jesus in the most violent way possible.

Not with faith.
Not with worship.
Not with humility.
He came with a weapon.
And yet he stood inches away from the greatest sacrifice the world has ever known.
This is both powerful and sobering.
Because it reveals something that still happens today.
You can be very close to Jesus… and still not truly see Him.
Some people are close to church.
Close to sermons.
Close to worship songs.
Close to Scripture.
But their hearts remain untouched.
They stand near the cross, but never surrender to it.
The Roman soldier reminds us that proximity to Jesus does not automatically mean transformation.
You can stand at the foot of the cross and still miss what it means.
But there is another side to this story.
And it is full of hope.
Because Jesus is so powerful that even those who approach Him wrongly can still encounter truth.
The soldier approached with a spear.
But what flowed from Jesus was not judgment.
It was evidence.

Evidence of sacrifice.
Evidence of love.
Evidence that even in suffering, Jesus was still giving.
Even in death, He was still pouring out.
That wound became a witness.
And it still is today.
Every time we talk about the cross, we are talking about a love that kept giving even after the world had done its worst.
Think about it.
Jesus had already been beaten.
Already mocked.
Already nailed to the cross.
Already hanging there in agony.
And still humanity gave Him one more wound.
Yet from that wound came something powerful.
Blood and water.
A reminder that even when the world pierced Him, He still poured out life.
That is the heart of the Gospel.
The world gave Him violence.
He gave the world redemption.
And maybe the most challenging part of this story is the question it leaves us with.
Which person are we at the cross?
Are we like the crowd, watching from a distance?
Are we like the religious leaders, hardened and unmoved?
Or are we like the soldier — close enough to touch the cross, yet not fully understanding what we are seeing?
Because it is possible to be near Jesus and still remain unchanged.
Near His name.
Near His story.
Near His sacrifice.
But still distant in the heart.
And that is a dangerous place to be.
The cross was never meant to be background information.
It was meant to confront us.
To break our pride.
To expose our need for mercy.
To show us how far God was willing to go to redeem us.
That soldier thought he was confirming death.
But what he witnessed was something far greater.
He was standing in front of the moment that would change the course of history forever.
The moment where love refused to stop.
The moment where sacrifice spoke louder than cruelty.
The moment where even a spear could not silence the message of salvation.
And maybe that is the real lesson.
No matter how broken the moment seems…
No matter how dark the scene looks…
When Jesus is involved, even wounds can become witnesses.
Even suffering can reveal purpose.
Even the place of death can become the doorway to life.
The soldier came with a spear.
But what flowed from Jesus revealed the heart of God.
And two thousand years later, that same truth is still reaching hearts.
Still changing lives.
Still calling people to look again at the cross.
Because what flowed from Jesus that day was not just blood and water.
It was the story of redemption written in sacrifice.
And anyone who truly sees it will never look at the cross the same way again.

John 19:34
“But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.”
